title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
summary:
Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities".
There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight.
On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.

title: Andy Burnham says he wants to 'repair bridges' between Ukraine and US
summary:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States, ahead of a meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street.
It comes after President Donald Trump said he had struck a deal with Moscow to import Russian diesel.
Burnham is expected to use the visit to promise further sanctions against Russia, while also announcing the UK will accelerate its delivery of air defence missiles to Kyiv.
It is Zelensky's second visit to the UK since Burnham became prime minister.
While other world leaders have received military welcomes, Number 10 said it could not find a record of one taking place on Downing Street.

title: Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire mean for Ukraine?
summary:
US President Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that an energy ceasefire had been reached between Ukraine and Russia that was "effective immediately".
Ukraine's President Zelensky responded by saying his country is willing to back an energy ceasefire if Russia does the same, adding it could "become a major step toward ending the war".
However, Moscow hasn't confirmed its agreement and Zelensky said Russia hit a Ukrainian power plant in Kharkiv "immediately after" Trump's post over the weekend.
The BBC's Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports from Kyiv, where Ukrainians are facing another winter with electricity outages that leave people without heat, light or even water.

title: Argentina targets UK in legal claim over Falklands oil exploration
summary:
The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles (209 km) from the Falkland Islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil.
The Falkland Islands government extended exploration licences last month and the field is expected to start pumping in 2028, potentially generating huge revenues for the roughly 3,500 inhabitants of the islands.
But the UK government insists Sea Lion is lawful, located on the Falkland Islands shelf and regulated by the islands' government.
While the Falkland Islands government grants exploration licences, they must be signed off by the UK Foreign Secretary.
Despite its defeat in 1982, Argentina has always maintained its right to the Falkland Islands.

title: Miliband says Britain won't tolerate threats on our soil, as Iran ambassador summoned
summary:
The foreign secretary has summoned the Iranian ambassador to make clear that "Britain will not tolerate threats on our soil" following last month's incident at RAF Fairford.
Ed Miliband said attempts by Iran to undermine the UK's security "through its criminal networks, proxy groups and state-backed malign activity is unacceptable".
Iran's ambassador to the UK, Seyed Ali Mousavi, said Tehran was not involved and was willing to cooperate with British authorities.
In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".
RAF Fairford, in the Cotswolds, has been used as a forward operating location by the US air force for decades.

title: US says China-linked hackers breached a regional organisation in Fiji
summary:
Hackers linked to China broke into the network of a regional group based in Suva, Fiji, the US Embassy in Fiji said on Monday.
Hackers tied to the Chinese state are going after governments, international bodies, and telecoms networks across the Pacific Islands, it said in a second post.
Stolen data gives Chinese spy agencies and others a view into private talks between Pacific Island countries, the embassy added.
The statement also raised concerns about crime, corruption, and foreign influence in the region, according to the Pacific Islands News Association.
In June, a China-linked botnet was found to have taken over 1,500 routers and devices.

title: It is inconceivable to think Russia did not try to interfere in Brexit vote, says PM
summary:
Andy Burnham has said it is "inconceivable" to think that Russia did not try to interfere in the 2016 EU referendum.
The prime minister told MPs he had not been questioning the legitimacy of the Brexit vote when he told the Rest is Politics podcast that it was "clear" there had been interference by Moscow.
His comments to the podcast provoked angry responses from some Brexit campaigners, with Reform UK leader Nigel Farage calling the prime minister "a liar".
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the prime minister had "implied that the referendum result was illegitimate because of Russian interference".
He also urged the prime minister to publish evidence of interference in the Brexit referendum as well as other UK votes.
